body:
You are drafting short lines of game text for a single-player D&D 2024 computer RPG set in Curse of Strahd's Barovia. Reply in plain text only. Do not message, route to, or ask anyone else; finish with your reply.

HOUSE RULES FOR ALL LINES
- ALLUDE, NEVER QUOTE. This game winks at another famous fantasy game in small ways, but no line may contain a name, quote, or catchphrase from another game, and no line may mention a game, a player, dice, rolls, levels or saving. Everything happens inside the world.
- The tone is gothic, dry and quietly funny, never cruel. The joke is in what is there.
- Give TWO options for every line so the editor can choose. Label each option A or B.
- Spoken lines are formatted: Speaker [mood]: Text   (mood optional: neutral, smile, angry, afraid, sad, sly, weary). One or two sentences a line.

THE NARRATOR (voice rules): an old gothic storyteller, fond of the party the way a gravedigger is fond of the weather: interested, no illusions. Second person, present tense ("You crouch..."), or the acting hero as {name}. One or two sentences; the second is usually the turn. Concrete senses, not adjectives. Never tells the player what to feel. No modern slang. When an animal speaks through the Speak with Animals spell, the Narrator reports it in quotes, in plain animal pictures (a dog says "the digger-man", "the box-maker").

THE PLACE: the Mad Mage's Hut high on Mount Baratok: a stone hut in the snow where a great wizard (Mordenkainen) has lived for forty years with his memory stolen. Real Narrator lines here: "A good silver mirror turned to face the wall. On its back, in chalk: DON'T." / "Equations in chalk cover the wall from floor to ceiling, beautiful and fluent, and every one of them stops halfway, at the same point, where the writer forgot what he was solving for." / "A hearth that has never had a fire in it. Frost grows on the firedogs like moss." / "A bed of wolf furs. The wolves, you notice, died of cold."

THE ORB: wrapped in the furs of the bed, a cracked glass orb the size of a fist, warm to the touch, humming faintly, with something violet moving slowly behind the cracks. Chalked on the cloth it is wrapped in, in the wizard's hand: "NOT MINE. A student's. Keep it fed. Keep it away from your chest." It hungers for magic. If the party gives it a spell scroll, it drinks the magic out of the scroll (the ink fades, the paper goes blank), purrs like a cat, and the hut's cold hearth lights itself for the first time and burns all night.
THE WIZARD, once his memory is restored (Mordenkainen): hard, proud, impatient, sardonic, an old and specific anger; short declarative sentences. Real lines: "My name is Mordenkainen." / "Everyone has questions. Very few have the right ones. Ask later." / "Make it brief. I have forty years of spellcraft to reconstruct in my head, and your pace is already distracting enough." / "Keep me away from mirrors and from anyone who says 'hush'."
Asked about the orb, he grumbles: it belonged to a young wizard from a city on the coast who had a habit of keeping the wrong things too close to his heart, literally; and the young man's teacher, a pipe-smoking old meddler with a beard, drops into other people's campfires uninvited and leaves them homework. Never name anyone.

WRITE:
1. NARRATOR, someone lifting the furs SUCCEEDS (Investigation): finding the orb and the chalked cloth. Two sentences, about 45 words.
2. NARRATOR, lifting the furs FAILS: only cold, stiff pelts. One sentence, under 25 words.
3. NARRATOR, first look at the orb in its cloth (when the party comes back to it). Two sentences, about 35 words.
4. NARRATOR, the party feeds it a spell scroll: the ink fading, the purr, the hearth lighting itself. Two or three sentences, under 55 words.
5. MORDENKAINEN, asked "Whose is it?": three short lines (each one or two sentences): the student; the student's chest; the pipe-smoking meddler of a teacher. Format: Mordenkainen: ...
6. NARRATOR, a second line for the cold hearth: a saucer of cream set out fresh on the hearthstone; up here, whatever comes for it must have wings. One or two sentences, under 30 words.

Return exactly this layout:
1A: Narrator: ...
1B: Narrator: ...
2A: Narrator: ...
2B: Narrator: ...
3A: Narrator: ...
3B: Narrator: ...
4A: Narrator: ...
4B: Narrator: ...
5A: Mordenkainen: ... | Mordenkainen: ... | Mordenkainen: ...
5B: Mordenkainen: ... | Mordenkainen: ... | Mordenkainen: ...
6A: Narrator: ...
6B: Narrator: ...
result:
1A: Narrator: Deep in the stiff pelts, your knuckles bump a linen bundle the size of a fist, unexpectedly warm, with a slow violet pulse moving behind cracked glass. On the cloth, a hand has chalked: "NOT MINE. A student's. Keep it fed. Keep it away from your chest."
1B: Narrator: {name} parts the frostbitten wolfskins and uncovers a cracked glass sphere wrapped in rag, humming against the palm while something violet turns sluggishly inside. Across the cloth, in urgent white chalk, is written: "NOT MINE. A student's. Keep it fed. Keep it away from your chest."
2A: Narrator: You turn over three stiff wolf pelts and find only frost, shed guard hairs, and the smell of old snow.
2B: Narrator: {name} shakes out the frozen furs, uncovering nothing warmer than grey hoarfrost and a few brittle winter ticks.
3A: Narrator: The cracked glass orb rests in its chalked rag, warm as a nesting hen and humming against your fingers. Behind the fractures, a knot of violet light turns over and waits.
3B: Narrator: Unwrapped from the furs, the fist-sized sphere warms the cold air an inch around it, its violet heart coiling slow behind the cracks. The chalked warning on the cloth rubs white onto your thumb.
4A: Narrator: The scroll touches the glass and the syllabic ink drains out of the parchment like water into sand, leaving the vellum blank and cold. From the cracked sphere comes a low, contented purr. Across the room, the frost on the firedogs snaps, and a clean yellow flame catches in the empty hearth.
4B: Narrator: Violet light presses against the cracks as the orb drinks the script straight off the parchment, until {name} is holding only a sheet of empty skin. The glass vibrates with a cat's thick purr. Behind you, the dead hearth sighs, and fire climbs the cold stones on its own.
5A: Mordenkainen [weary]: A young wizard from a harbor city down the coast, too clever by half and far too fond of high company. | Mordenkainen: He had a ruinous habit of keeping things he could not digest tucked right behind his breastbone. | Mordenkainen [angry]: His master—an old beard with a pipe and no respect for privacy—left it by my fire like a stray cat and vanished before I could throw it back.
5B: Mordenkainen: It belonged to an overeager boy from the Sword Coast who mistook appetite for ambition. | Mordenkainen [sly]: He kept his worst mistake lodged in his own chest, so I suppose a rag in my bed is an improvement. | Mordenkainen [weary]: His teacher is a pipe-smoking meddler who drops into other men's camps uninvited to hand out chores.
6A: Narrator: On the frozen hearthstone sits a saucer of fresh cream, not yet skinned over with ice. Up on this peak, whatever comes to lap it must arrive on wings.
6B: Narrator: Someone has set a clay saucer of unfrozen cream beside the cold firedogs. At this altitude, any housecat coming for it has feathers.
